thuy_vi: Thúy Vi Tông, the green-haze herb and pill sect of the south-west: robes of hemp dyed green-grey with haze-grown indigo, fine, clean and well fitted, the hems of the slope's disciples always damp and darker; outer-gate disciples add a plain grey sash, inner-gate disciples a pale green silk collar and a dark green cord, true disciples and elders a green silk sash; the Cliff Hall (ridge faction) wears dry undyed hemp, stiff and pale, with no green; small tools at the belt: needle case, herb pouch, seed gourd.
muc_van: Mục Vân Trang, the cloud-herder horse manor of the western plain: well-made felt coats in grass-brown and undyed wool with horn toggles and standing collars, sheepskin collars and linings in winter, riders' fingerless leather gloves and boots, a faded festival ribbon braided into the hair of anyone who has won at the lord's festival, wool scarves; clean, thick and practical, never ragged.
chuc_ha: Chức Hà Các, the Pavilion of the Woven Clouds, a silk-weaving sect of the south: fine undyed cream silk robes, clean and pressed, narrow sleeves tied back with cord for work; outer-gate disciples a pale beige sash, inner disciples a grey-green sash, fire-setters a deep red sash and a lacquered shuttle through the hair, elders a grey-green sash edged with red; burn-pale fingertips and silk thread tools (reels, needles, shuttles) are the marks of the trade.
thu_phan: Thu Phần Các, the Pavilion of the Autumn Graves, soul-singers of the ruined thunder city: undyed hemp mourning robes worn for life, of good clean cloth, crossed collars and wide sleeves, a white hemp cord at the waist; singers add an ash-grey sash, elders a black band at hem and cuff; small bronze bell charms; plain, pale and sombre, never ragged.
suong_tung: Sương Tùng Các, the Pavilion of Frost and Pine, talisman writers of the pine lake: undyed linen robes, clean and soft, with ink dark to the second knuckle and on the cuffs; outer-gate disciples a pale grey sash, inner-gate disciples a pine-green sash, the head and elders a dark green sash; birch-bark hats in the paper yards, brushes, ink sticks and paper lanterns carried unlit by day.
